plain_english: Why do we complain about Nature? She has been kind to us. Life is long enough — if you know how to use it.
original_excerpt: Why do we complain of Nature? she has dealt kindly with us. Life is long enough, if you know how to use it.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 2

plain_english: One man is driven by greed that can never be satisfied. Another wastes his energy on completely pointless tasks. Another drowns himself in wine. Another is paralyzed by laziness. One man exhausts himself chasing ambition, desperately trying to win people's approval. Another becomes a merchant and travels to every corner of the world, hoping to get rich. source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 2

plain_english: They chase after powerful people who will never return their loyalty. Many spend their time either trying to grab other people's money or whining about their own situation. A huge number have no clear goals at all. They drift from one half-baked plan to another, restless and never satisfied with anything. Some people don't care enough about any goal to actually pursue it. They just lie around lazily until fate catches up with them. So I have no doubt that the greatest poet was right when he wrote those words like a prophecy: 'We live only a small part of our lives.'
original_excerpt: unrequited service of great men: many are occupied either in laying claim to other men's fortune or in complaining of their own: a great number have no settled purpose, and are tossed from one new scheme to another by a rambling, inconsistent, dissatisfied, fickle habit of mind: some care for no object sufficiently to try to attain it, but lie lazily yawning until their fate comes upon them: so that I cannot doubt the truth of that verse which the greatest of poets has dressed in the guise of an oracular response— "We live a small part only of our lives."
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 2

plain_english: But all duration is time, not life. Vices press in on us from every side. They don't let us get back on our feet or lift our heads to see the truth. When we're down, they keep us flat on the ground, chained to shallow desires. People trapped like this never get a chance to find themselves. Even when they get a brief break, they roll back and forth like the ocean that keeps heaving and tossing after a storm. They never get any rest from their cravings.
original_excerpt: But all duration is time, not life: vices press upon us and surround us on every side, and do not permit us to regain our feet, or to raise our eyes and gaze upon truth, but when we are down keep us prostrate and chained to low desires. Men who are in this condition are never allowed to come to themselves: if ever by chance they obtain any rest, they roll to and fro like the deep sea, which heaves and tosses after a gale, and they never have any respite from their lusts.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 2

plain_english: You think I'm only talking about people with obvious problems? No, look at those everyone envies — the successful ones. They're drowning in their own good fortune. How many rich people are crushed by their wealth? How many speakers have died because they couldn't stop showing off how clever they were? How many have made themselves sick with constant pleasure-seeking? How many have lost all freedom because they're surrounded by crowds of people wanting favors? Look at everyone, from bottom to top. This man calls friends to help him. That one appears in court. Another defends himself. Someone else argues his case. Another sits on the jury. But nobody claims time for himself. Everyone wastes their life on someone else.
original_excerpt: Do you suppose that I speak of those whose ills are notorious? Nay, look at those whose prosperity all men run to see: they are choked by their own good things. To how many men do riches prove a heavy burden? how many men's eloquence and continual desire to display their own cleverness has cost them their lives? how many are sallow with constant sensual indulgence? how many have no freedom left them by the tribe of clients that surges around them? Look through all these, from the lowest to the highest:—this man calls his friends to support him, this one is present in court, this one is the defendant, this one pleads for him, this one is on the jury: but no one lays claim to his own self, every one wastes his time over some one else.
source_reference: On the Shortness of Life, Section 2
